facts.text: The Horne Smelter in Rouyn-Noranda, owned by Glencore, is Canada's only copper smelter and the largest processor of metals from electronic scrap in North America.
facts.evidence: The Horne Smelter is located in Rouyn-Noranda, Quebec, and is owned by Glencore (since 2013). It is Canada's only copper smelter and the largest processor of metals from electronic scrap in North America.

facts.text: Glencore suspended about $1 billion in planned Horne smelter investments in February 2026 after talks with the Quebec government stalled.

overview: Rouyn-Noranda had 42,313 residents in the 2021 Census, nearly unchanged from 42,334 in 2016. The city covers 5,963.57 square kilometres, so its territory stretches well beyond the urban core into villages such as Cadillac, Évain and Mont-Brun.

Mining and metal processing anchor the economy, led by the Horne Smelter, with a university and regional services adding stable employment. Local businesses compete for a steady population that earns mining wages, travels long distances and expects reliable service.
